```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(easyNIS)
```

## Define discharge outcomes

Use `nis_outcomes()` on numeric NIS Core fields before building a survey
design. It adds three columns and leaves the query in DuckDB. The example
uses invented discharges.

Negative HCUP missing-value sentinels and non-integer values become
`NA` in the derived outcomes.

```{r design}
outcomes <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2024)) |>
  nis_outcomes()

design <- nis_design(
  outcomes,
  cohort = TRUE,
  keep = c(in_hospital_death, los_days, discharge_disposition, TOTCHG, CCR_NIS),
  dollars = 2024
)
```

- **In-hospital mortality.** `in_hospital_death` is a logical indicator from
  `DIED`. A discharge alive has value `FALSE`. Missing or invalid `DIED`
  stays missing even when a disposition is recorded. The event is death
  during the sampled hospitalization. [HCUP DIED notes](https://hcup-us.ahrq.gov/db/vars/died/nisnote.jsp)
- **Length of stay.** `los_days` uses HCUP's edited `LOS` in whole days,
  including zero for admission and discharge on the same date. Deaths and
  transfers can have recorded LOS for the sampled stay. [HCUP LOS notes](https://hcup-us.ahrq.gov/db/vars/los/nisnote.jsp)
- **Discharge disposition.** `discharge_disposition` holds the numeric
  `DISPUNIFORM` code. After collection, `nis_label()` or `nis_design()`
  applies the factor labels.
  Code 2 denotes transfer to a short-term hospital. Code 5 covers several
  types of other facilities, including skilled nursing and intermediate
  care. Code 6 includes home health, home IV, and home hospice. Codes 21
  (court/law enforcement) and 99 (alive with destination unknown) are valid
  categories. An invalid or missing code yields a missing disposition. [HCUP DISPUNIFORM notes](https://hcup-us.ahrq.gov/db/vars/dispuniform/nisnote.jsp)

These are Core fields on both sides of the 2015 ICD transition. Review
the source year's coding before pooling releases. Historical `DISP` and
detailed billing disposition fields use different codes.

## Choose an estimator

For mortality, the survey-weighted mean of the indicator is the proportion
of discharges with known status that ended in death. For disposition, use
survey-weighted category proportions and state whether the denominator
includes in-hospital deaths and the known-alive, unknown-destination group.
For skewed LOS, survey quantiles give the median and the 25th and 75th
percentiles while retaining same-day stays.

```{r estimates}
dplyr::summarise(design, mortality = srvyr::survey_mean(in_hospital_death, na.rm = TRUE))
survey::svymean(~discharge_disposition, design, na.rm = TRUE)
survey::svyquantile(~los_days, design, c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75), na.rm = TRUE)
```

A geometric mean of LOS requires positive values for the log. If the
question concerns positive stays, define that survey domain explicitly
and exponentiate its weighted mean log LOS and confidence limits. Report
the share of same-day stays and the rule used for zeros. Adding a constant
to all stays changes the scale of the quantity being estimated. A NIS
heart failure study reported geometric means after substituting a small
positive value for zeros, an analysis choice to document when reproducing
that study. [Heart failure utilization study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6676288/)

## Define and audit a timed procedure outcome

A secondary diagnosis marks a condition recorded during the stay. Even
with POA information, its slot gives no date relative to an index
procedure. For a procedure-based outcome, use the day recorded for its
matched procedure slot. The example uses two timing rules on invented
discharges. Both outcome procedures have the same recorded code, and only
the first has a known day.

```{r timed-outcomes}
timing_cases <- data.frame(
  YEAR = 2020L,
  I10_DX1 = "I509",
  I10_DX2 = "N179",
  I10_PR1 = "02703ZZ",
  I10_PR2 = "0JH60DZ",
  PRDAY1 = 1L,
  PRDAY2 = c(1L, NA_integer_)
)
day_audit <- nis_audit_prday(timing_cases, pr = "0JH60")
day_audit

timed <- timing_cases |>
  nis_flag_dx(recorded_aki = "N17", position = "secondary") |>
  nis_flag_pr_timing(
    index_pr = "02703", outcome_pr = "0JH60",
    name = "on_or_after", relation = "on_or_after", missing_day = "indeterminate"
  ) |>
  nis_flag_pr_timing(
    index_pr = "02703", outcome_pr = "0JH60",
    name = "strictly_after", relation = "after", missing_day = "indeterminate"
  )
timed[c("PRDAY1", "PRDAY2", "on_or_after", "strictly_after", "recorded_aki")]
```

The same-day case meets the on-or-after definition. The strict-after
definition excludes it. The missing-day case is unknown under both rules.
The secondary acute kidney injury code is recorded in both cases and has
unknown timing relative to the procedure. State the code sets, slots,
timing rule, and missing-day treatment. Report how many matched slots have
known days and how many discharges enter each timing analysis.

## Report costs and the analysis denominator

`nis_design(..., dollars = 2024)` uses the same adjustment as
`nis_cost()` to calculate `cost_adj` from charges and the hospital
cost-to-charge ratio. Report the price index and reference dollar year.
Use a survey-weighted arithmetic mean for cost per discharge or a
survey-weighted median and quartiles for the distribution of costs.

```{r cost}
survey::svymean(~cost_adj, design, na.rm = TRUE)
nis_cost_provenance(design)$base_year
```

For resource use across all discharges, include stays ending in death
when LOS or cost is observed. A survivor-only analysis answers a different
question. For example, a study of craniotomy costs excluded in-hospital
deaths and stays with withdrawal of care, while a pulmonary disease study
estimated LOS and costs specifically for stays ending in death. State
which population each summary describes. [Craniotomy cost study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4351828/) · [End-of-life pulmonary hospitalization study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11251072/)

Check and report missingness by outcome and comparison group before using
`na.rm = TRUE`. Each summary then uses its own observed-outcome denominator.
Missing or invalid charges or CCRs can leave cost unobserved even for stays
with known LOS. A complete-cost summary describes the discharges with
calculable costs. If missingness differs by year, group, or survival status,
assess how that affects comparisons and any inference to all discharges.
One NIS study of prolonged stays used weighted medians and quartiles for
non-normal outcomes and complete cases for its mortality regression. [Prolonged hospitalization study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5362287/)

See [Charges, costs, and provenance](costs.html) and
[Disclosure review](disclosure.html) before reporting results.
